readerQuestion: Should I use HACS, Apps, or Add integration to add a Home Assistant feature, and what should I do when the thing I downloaded does not appear?
directAnswer: Start with a built-in integration for supported devices. Use Apps to run companion software on Home Assistant OS, and HACS for a particular community extension. Get HACS is only a downloader app; after its instructions and restart, add the HACS integration and authorize it with GitHub. Container can use HACS but has no managed Apps store. Finish each project's own configuration and check a harmless temperature card before changing household controls.
originalContribution: Section 5 gives a three-request worksheet for Mushroom, Adaptive Lighting and MQTT, showing installation sequence, expected completion evidence and what that evidence does not prove. Section 6 supplies a reversible built-in-versus-Mushroom temperature-card comparison on two clients. The final decision table distinguishes a missing store, unfinished HACS setup, a pending restart, a card mistaken for an integration and an app with no configured device connection.
limitations: This is documentation research and an automated editorial review, not a human/expert review or a tested Home Assistant installation. No extension was installed on a real household server; the temperature-card check is a proposed acceptance procedure. Menu labels and project requirements can change. The generated cover is visibly disclosed as an editorial illustration. The review does not establish indexing or search performance. Source-link and local-site checks validate availability and rendering, not every supported device or extension.

claimChecks.claim: Home Assistant renamed add-ons to Apps in 2026.2. The Mosquitto app and MQTT integration perform different jobs; a missing old Add-ons label alone does not show a broken installation.
Apps run alongside Home Assistant and their managed installation is supported on Home Assistant OS. HACS does not add Supervisor or the App Store to Container.

HACS is not an app and contains no Home Assistant Apps. Its prerequisites include configuration/log access and connectivity to its distribution services; a downloaded project's version requirements can be stricter.

OS uses the hacs/addons repository and Get HACS downloader app; Container uses the procedure inside the running Home Assistant container. Both proceed to restart and integration configuration. Legacy tabs do not establish current Home Assistant installation support.
HACS initial setup requires Add integration and GitHub device authorization after download/restart; hard refresh or clearing the browser cache addresses the documented missing-list issue.
Downloaded custom integrations need their own configuration, which may use the UI or YAML. Not every HACS download should appear in Add integration.

HACS dashboard elements are served as card resources, separate from custom server integrations. The documented Open source check distinguishes served JavaScript from a 404 before changing sensor setup.

Mushroom is a card collection with a HACS download path and dashboard editor configuration. The suggested temperature check uses an existing sensor and a built-in comparison card; it does not test hardware control or add a sensor integration.

Adaptive Lighting's documented installation proceeds through HACS, restart and integration configuration, then selected existing lights. Its detailed control settings remain in the established Tara guide.
HACS custom elements are not reviewed or tested by the Home Assistant development team; their presence in HACS is not a technical testing endorsement.

A running MQTT broker alone does not establish a configured MQTT device or an entity in Home Assistant. The integration must connect to the broker and the device needs the appropriate configuration/discovery.
